newsitem.title: USA: Costello sees Australian inflation below 3.0 pct.
newsitem.headline: Costello sees Australian inflation below 3.0 pct.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello said he expects the country's inflation to drop below its current three percent level.
While declining to specify a timeframe for inflation to fall, Costello asserted the Australian government has dedicated itself to holding down domestic price growth.
"At present, inflation in Australia is three percent and we expect it to go lower," Costello said in remarks to the Asia Society here.
"The government is committed to locking in low inflation, and locking in low inflation expectations," he added.
Turning to Australia's current budget projections, Costello said the government plans to eliminate the federal deficit over the next two years.
In the 1996-97 fiscal year, Australia should shave its deficit to 1.1 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) from 2.1 in the current fiscal year, Costello predicts.
In 1997-98 the budget should be "near balanced" and in 1998-99 should post a "small" surplus," Costello added.
